flags.finding: [partially supported] Scene S040 depicts a full-contact street hockey game staged entirely on the flat rooftop of an active commercial convenience store building. Performers and background actors ascend an exterior ladder, skate without perimeter barriers, execute aggressive body checks and slide tackles, shoot balls over the unprotected roof edge, and peer down from the ledge. Operating an un-railed elevated set with active physical sports choreography poses severe fall-from-height and impact hazards for both cast and camera crew. Under CSATF Safety Bulletin #4 and OSHA elevated workplace safety standards, the production must implement mandatory fall protection systems, edge safety perimeter netting or catch rigs, harness line rigging for edge proximity shots, and dedicated stunt coordination for all skating impact stunts and ladder ascents.

flags.finding: [partially supported] The screenplay features pervasive hard profanity throughout, totaling 88 script-wide occurrences of 'fuck' and its variants across 25 scenes (S001, S018, S019, S020, S021, S024, S028, S030, S036, S038, S039, S040, S042, S046, S047, S048, S049, S051, S056, S058, S059, S060, S061, S062, S064), 45 occurrences of 'shit', and numerous harsh epithets including 'cunt' (S028, S055) and homophobic slurs ('faggot' in S018). Under CARA guidelines, more than one harsh sexually-derived expletive requires an R rating, and using such terms in explicit sexual contexts reinforces a restrictive rating band. Pervasive vulgar language alone mandates an R rating.

citations.title: CARA outlines the criteria for rating a movie G, PG, PG-13, ...
citations.excerpt: A motion picture's single use of one of the harsher sexually-derived words, though only as an expletive, initially requires at least a PG-13 rating. More than one such expletive requires an R rating, as must even one of those words used in a sexual context.

remedy.detail: To target a lower rating band such as PG-13, cut 87 of the 88 uses of 'fuck', eliminate all instances of 'cunt' and 'faggot', and replace vulgar sexual slurs with non-explicit dialogue.

flags.finding: [partially supported] The script contains explicit depiction and dialogue of commercial illicit drug dealing and substance preparation. In S018, Jay openly solicits sales of controlled substances ('hits, hash, weed, and later on I'll have 'shrooms') outside the convenience store. In S049, Jay negotiates hash transactions with a customer ('For this kind of hash, you need that kind of cash'). In S060, Jay buys rolling papers, receives marijuana from Silent Bob, and actively rolls a joint inside the store while celebrating cocaine, weed, and alcohol consumption ('smoking weed! Doing coke! Drinking beers!'). Under CARA classification rules, drug abuse and dealing are core adult elements that trigger an automatic R rating.

citations.title: CARA outlines the criteria for rating a movie G, PG, PG-13, ...
citations.excerpt: An R-rated motion picture, in the view of the Rating Board, contains some adult material. An R-rated motion picture may include adult themes, adult activity, hard language, intense or persistent violence, sexually-oriented nudity, drug abuse or other elements, so that parents are counseled to take this rating very seriously.

remedy.detail: Cut or replace the illicit drug distribution dialogue, references to hash/cocaine/shrooms, and active joint rolling in S018, S049, and S060 with benign street loitering dialogue.

flags.finding: [partially supported] Scene S040 depicts a full-contact street hockey game staged entirely on the flat rooftop of an active commercial convenience store building. Performers and background actors ascend an exterior ladder, skate without perimeter barriers, execute aggressive body checks and slide tackles, shoot balls over the unprotected roof edge, and peer down from the ledge. Operating an un-railed elevated set with active physical sports choreography poses severe fall-from-height and impact hazards for both cast and camera crew. Under CSATF Safety Bulletin #4 and OSHA elevated workplace safety standards, the production must implement mandatory fall protection systems, edge safety perimeter netting or catch rigs, harness line rigging for edge proximity shots, and dedicated stunt coordination for all skating impact stunts and ladder ascents.

citations.title: INDUSTRY WIDE LABOR-MANAGEMENT SAFETY COMMITTEE SAFETY BULLETIN #4 STUNTS
citations.excerpt: All equipment used for rigging must be inspected to check for wear, damage, and integrity prior to use. The Stunt Coordinator should approve the use of all rigging equipment. Any equipment found to be defective shall be removed from service. Fall protection may be required when rigging at heights.

remedy.detail: Hire a SAG-AFTRA certified Stunt Coordinator and key rigging grip to design and install perimeter fall arrest / safety catch systems, inspect ladder mounting and roof decking integrity, choreograph skating tackles with padded stunt doubles, and conduct pre-shoot rooftop safety walkthroughs with all cast and crew under CSATF Safety Bulletin #4. Cost and crew rates vary by shooting region and union agreements.

flags.finding: [partially supported] Scenes S019, S028, and S036 feature minor child performers and atmospheric chemical hazards in enclosed retail spaces. S019 depicts the practical discharge of a pressurized fire extinguisher ('white powder explodes over the throng') in an enclosed retail interior, which creates chemical particulate respiratory hazards requiring certified prop/SFX powder substitutes (such as food-grade starch/talc) and adequate ventilation. S028 features a small child in close proximity while explicit adult pornographic titles are recited aloud and the child repeats vulgar language, requiring strict child welfare and psychological safeguarding protocols. S036 depicts a minor ('can't be any more than five') purchasing cigarettes, placing a cigarette in her mouth, and receiving matches. State child labor laws and SAG-AFTRA Young Performer regulations mandate credentialed studio teachers/welfare workers, strict working hour limitations, non-toxic inert prop cigarettes/matches with no ignition capability, and strict shielding of minor performers from sexually explicit or harmful material.

citations.title: State Statutes | SAG-AFTRA
citations.excerpt: Child performers below 16 years of age must be accompanied throughout the work day by a responsible person. In areas covered by SAG-AFTRA’s jurisdiction, the responsible person is the parent or someone named by the parent.

citations.title: State Statutes | SAG-AFTRA
citations.excerpt: Employers are required to provide time and facilities for the education of child performers, regardless of where they are schooled, when their work schedules prevent them from fulfilling their educational requirement outside of work. Employers must provide certified or credentialed on-location teachers when needed.

remedy.detail: Retain a certified Studio Teacher / Child Welfare Worker to oversee minor performers on set in S028 and S036, enforce statutory work-hour restrictions and parental accompaniment, use inert non-toxic prop cigarettes and safety matches with no sulfur heads, and in S019 utilize only non-toxic, hypoallergenic SFX dust/particulate spray supervised by a licensed SPFX coordinator with full interior ventilation. Costs vary by shooting region and union agreements.

flags.finding: [partially supported] Scene S064 depicts an intensive, multi-phase physical brawl between Dante and Randal inside a cramped convenience store. Staged actions include throat-choking to the ground, body punches throwing a performer into a metal magazine rack, falling violently into bakery shelving, striking the head with food props, tackling into store aisles, toppling shelving units, and spraying a commercial aerosol product (FDS feminine deodorant spray) directly into a performer's eyes and face. These physical actions present substantial risks of blunt-force trauma, lacerations from retail shelving or displaced merchandise, spinal/neck injury during choking and hard floor falls, and chemical eye irritation/corneal damage from practical aerosol discharge. Staging this sequence requires professional stunt coordination, engineered breakaway props, personal protective padding, and specialized eye-safe spray rigs.

citations.title: INDUSTRY WIDE LABOR-MANAGEMENT SAFETY COMMITTEE SAFETY BULLETIN #4 STUNTS
citations.excerpt: The Stunt Coordinator will review the PPE with Production Management and/or the designated representative to ensure studio requirements are followed. No one in Production Management should pressure the Performer or the Stunt Coordinator to scale back the use of protective equipment.

remedy.detail: Retain a SAG-AFTRA certified Stunt Coordinator to choreograph and rehearse all fight action, supply stunt doubles for floor throws and shelf impacts, reinforce or construct rubber/breakaway retail fixtures and foam food props, and replace commercial aerosol cans with a dedicated SFX prop delivering sterile water or saline aerosol mist under CSATF Safety Bulletin #4. Costs vary by shooting region and union agreements.

flags.finding: Multiple scenes feature live domestic animals in direct physical action and environmental exposure. S001 depicts an actor physically wrestling with a pet dog on a bed. S005 depicts the dog lapping up a spill of chocolate milk from the floor; chocolate contains theobromine, which is toxic and potentially fatal to canines, presenting a direct ingestion hazard if staged practically with real confectionery. S009, S025, S029, and S038 feature a live domestic cat ('Lenin's Tomb') picked up and handled by actors, placed directly on commercial checkout counters, and shown inside a litter box during a staged elimination gag. Live animals on set are vulnerable to stress, startling from crew/lighting movements, sanitation hazards, and escape risks in open retail/exterior door environments. Production must comply with CSATF Safety Bulletin #6 and American Humane on-set animal welfare standards.

citations.title: SAFETY BULLETINS RECOMMENDED BY INDUSTRY WIDE LABOR-MANAGEMENT
citations.excerpt: Animals are unpredictable. If animals are used in filming, the Animal Handler should meet with cast and crew and inform them of the safety procedures in effect and answer any questions. Safety meetings should be held when appropriate. Do not feed, pet or play with any animal without the permission and direct supervision of its trainer. Defer to the animal trainers at all times.

remedy.detail: Retain a professional, certified Animal Handler / Wrangler to supervise all canine and feline staging, maintain a quiet closed set during animal takes, secure escape routes, and ensure animal safety; in S005, strictly replace real chocolate milk with a veterinary-approved non-toxic canine-safe substitute (such as diluted carob powder or goat milk with food coloring); in S029, use clean, sanitized artificial litter props under CSATF Safety Bulletin #6. Costs vary by shooting region and union agreements.

flags.finding: In S033, dialogue between Randal and Dante analyzes the Galactic Empire from Return of the Jedi as an evil theocracy, explicitly comparing Emperor Palpatine to 'the pope for the dark side of the Force' as an 'evil holy man' and asserting that the rebel forces were Catholics fighting religious persecution. Under UAE Media Council content guidelines, content deemed disrespectful or trivializing to established divinely-revealed religions and religious leadership can trigger censorship intervention or mandatory dialogue adjustment.

flags.finding: In S036, Randal unfolds an adult magazine centerfold described explicitly in stage directions as showing spread vaginal lips and anus, and in S055 he screens explicit pornography in a video store. Under BBFC Classification Guidelines, clear, uncensored visual depiction of real explicit sexual organs / hardcore pornographic material cannot be accommodated within a standard theatrical or home video '18' certificate and is restricted to the legally segregated 'R18' classification (only available in licensed adult venues). To maintain a standard commercial 18 certificate in the UK, graphic explicit genital imagery must not be shown on camera.

citations.title: BBFC | BBFC
citations.excerpt: Pornography containing clear images of real sex, strong fetish material, sexually explicit animated images, or other very strong sexual images will be confined to the R18 category. Material that is unacceptable in pornography at R18 is also unacceptable in pornography at 18.

remedy.detail: Ensure camera angles, props, or post-production optical framing keep the centerfold in S036 and the television monitor in S055 free from explicit real genital/hardcore imagery so the film qualifies for a standard BBFC 18 rating.

flags.finding: In scene S001, Frank Miller's graphic novel 'The Dark Knight Returns' (published by DC Comics) is explicitly listed on Dante's bedroom bookshelf alongside classic literature. Displaying recognizable copyrighted graphic novel cover art and trade dress on camera as set dressing engages visual artwork reproduction rights (Ringgold v. BET). Although background set dressing is often considered low risk, prominent graphic elements on modern publications require clearance or replacement.
